g.text: A recurring view of one set of metrics

svg.text: Hold extra Japan ad spend: fix conversion first, then scale in steps against an
Should we raise Japan’s ad budget by 50% in H1 2026?
Not yet. Spend six weeks restoring conversion on the top five ASINs; once it is back to 2024 levels and ACOS ≤
Japan’s monthly sales fell 8% over 2025, the only declining marketplace of six (Exhibit 1).
The decline is conversion-led: all five top ASINs converted worse, by up to 2.7 points (Exhibit 2).
At today’s conversion, +50% budget would cut profit by about US$120k; each conversion point adds about US$170k (Exhibit 3).
Five of six marketplaces trended up in 2025; Japan was the only decline
Monthly sales by marketplace (US$ 10k), 2025; common y-axis
Note: All panels share the same y-axis.
Conversion fell for all five top Japan ASINs, by up to 2.7
Conversion rate of Japan’s top-5 ASINs (%), 2024 vs 2025
Note: Axis does not start at zero; read the gaps, not bar lengths.
Conversion drives Japan’s profit most; extra ad spend
Japan operating profit, H1 2026E (US$ 10k), one-at-a-time changes
Note: (1) “Ad budget +50%” is the adverse case at today’s conversion (ACOS rises); flat budget is
the base; (2) Sorted by swing; other drivers held at base.
Rank may slip during the fix; keep base bids on core keywords.
If competitors cut prices sharply in Q1, revisit the price assumptions.
Weeks 1–2: main-image, title and price A/B tests on the top five ASINs.
Weeks 3–6: review conversion and ACOS; unlock the first +15% if the gate is met.

g.text: One decision, its evidence and a clear call

svg.text: Example study: compound B is the most potent in vitro and slows tumour
Evidence from viability assays, xenografts and transcriptomics
We compared three compounds for inhibition of tumour-cell viability at 72 h and assessed
compound B’s efficacy and transcriptomic response in a subcutaneous xenograft model.
Compound B had an IC50 of 7.38 nM, about 7.6× the reference (Exhibit 1). By day 21, mean
tumour volume was 68% lower at 30 mg/kg and 44% lower at 10 mg/kg than with vehicle
(Exhibit 2). Treated and control profiles separated completely on the first principal component
(Exhibit 3), with 77 genes significantly up- and 65 down-regulated (Exhibit 4). The data are
illustrative and show the study-report format.
Compound B’s IC50 is 7.38 nM (95% CI 6.18–8.80), about 7.6× the reference (Exhibit 1).
Inhibition is dose-dependent: day-21 tumour volume is 68% lower at 30 mg/kg and 44%
The transcriptome responds clearly: PC1 (41.3% of variance) fully separates control from
77 genes are significantly up- and 65 down-regulated; the first clustering split separates
All three compounds show sigmoidal concentration–response curves; compound B’s curve is shifted left (lower IC50).
Compound B is the most potent (IC50 7.38 nM), about 7.6× the reference
Tumour cell viability at 72 h (% of vehicle), 10 concentrations, triplicate wells

Note: (1) Four-parameter logistic fit on all replicates (least squares); IC50/EC50 = concentration at the midpoint between fitted top and bottom; 95% CI from the standard error of log IC50 (t distribution);
(2) Points = mean ± SD, n = 3 per concentration.
Mean tumour volume in both dose groups falls increasingly behind vehicle over time, more so at the high dose.
At day 21, 30 mg/kg cut mean tumour volume by 68% vs vehicle; 10 mg/kg by 44%
Subcutaneous xenograft volume (mm³), once-daily oral dosing, 8 mice per group
Note: (1) Volume = length × width² / 2; (2) Points are means of replicates; bars = ±SEM; n = 8 per point; groups offset slightly for legibility.
Treatment shifts the expression of many genes, and samples cluster by treatment group.
